acceptanceCriteria: The owner decides whether dogfood check should bind the recorded impact --root to the checked worktree on both the abstention and the non-abstention path, or on neither, and the decision is recorded in docs/specs/daily-change-evidence-workflow-v0.md with a stable requirement ID.
If the rule changes, internal/dogfoodflow/check.go and its tests enforce the same root binding on both paths, and a relocated worktree copy gets the same result whether impact abstained or not.
body: dogfood check binds the recorded impact argv root to the checked worktree only when impact abstains: argvRecorded (internal/dogfoodflow/check.go:262-274) requires argv[2] to be the same directory as c.root, so a worktree copied to another path fails context-abstention-evidence-drift. The non-abstention path does not compare the root. Found while freezing the V1-0019 go-chi/chi case, where impact abstains on a foreign repository and the harness's copy-based loop controls failed; the harness now restores and runs variants in place. Question: is the asymmetry intended (abstention evidence is bound to the directory that produced it) or should both paths bind or neither?
title: Decide whether dogfood check binds the impact root on both paths or only on abstention
